chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Cozy's Conception of Carmen on Everest without payment
summary: Cole sees his MGM-era record reissued by Everest under a changed title and was never paid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Oh yeah, they're bootlegging them like the devil yes. I look at a lot of my Carmen things.
I see them on labels that I don't even know. Like that Cozy Conception of Carmen.
Hold on a second. I just handed Cozy a copy of a record--it's now on Everest Records, and it was originally called Cozy's Conception of Carmen. For what label?
Oh Charlie Parkie, MGM label.
Right, and that was recorded in '61.
Yeah.
And that's now what? Everest FS 288, that's one you said you didn't know anything about it.
I didn't know anything about it when I first saw it.
Did you ever get paid for it?
No.
Not a penny, huh?
Not one penny. I don't even know where to-- where are they? Where do they originate?
Their address is listed at 10920 Wilshire Boulevard, Suite 410, Los Angeles, California.
Now who should you contact there?
I haven't the foggiest.
Yeah, that's the thing.

But I do know that they've bought up masters from various small companies like, you know, Charlie Parker Records, and that's where they get the masters and they put them out. So, but you didn't know a thing about it.
I didn't know anything about that.
Had you ever seen that record before in the shops at all?

No, a student brought that same record by and showed it to me, but I didn't know anything about it. Last one I saw was up there on MGM. This is new. Now of course the only thing that they eliminated on this one, it wasn't a Cozy Conception of Carmen, it's just Cozy Cole.
Yeah, different title.
So see, that's how they beat that rap.
Really. Although you're still entitled to royalties....
Oh of course.
Try to get some.
Yeah, yeah. You've got to fight for it and get a lawyer.
Certainly.
You're liable to pay him more than you'll ever receive, you know, keep that going.
It's a big mess, no question.
It's too bad, too.
